PROMPT SHARE: The biggest AI breakthrough isn’t realism. It’s presence.

#AIVideo #Marketing #Advertising

The people, movement, noise and unpredictability give the world a sense of life beyond the camera.

That’s when generation starts becoming experience.

➜ Image Prompt:

Photography & Cinematography
Create an ultra-realistic nighttime street portrait with the raw, spontaneous look of early-2000s nightlife photography. Direct on-camera flash illuminates the subject sharply against a much darker city background, with natural grain, slight highlight blowout, deep shadows, imperfect exposure and authentic point-and-shoot character. No fake or plastic skin, no beauty filtering, no CGI or animated appearance.

Character & Pose
A striking young man with rugged, high-fashion model features, lean athletic build, sharply defined jawline and cheekbones, strong brows, full lips and short dark hair styled wet and tousled with loose curls falling onto his forehead. Natural pores, subtle facial texture and realistic imperfections. He sits casually on the edge of a city curb at night, legs spread asymmetrically, one knee raised toward the camera. One forearm rests loosely across the raised knee while his other hand reaches down beside him toward a small shaggy brown dog partially entering the bottom of the frame. He looks directly into the camera with a serious, confident expression.

Outfit
Fitted black long-sleeve turtleneck, faded distressed gray-blue jeans with worn areas and small rips, and a black leather belt. Silver pendant necklace, small hoop earring, chunky silver cuff bracelet, dark oversized wristwatch, and a thin bracelet. Styling feels slightly rebellious, understated and naturally lived-in rather than polished.

Environment
A busy urban nightlife street after dark. Several casually dressed people walk behind him, cropped naturally by the frame, while parked and passing cars create scattered headlights and small pools of distant light. The pavement is gritty and imperfect with curbs, cracks and ordinary street details visible. Keep the background activity believable and incidental—the image should feel like a real moment caught outside a club or late-night gathering, not a staged fashion shoot. Wide horizontal composition, intimate close-range flash photography, authentic real-world energy.

We turned Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, Pi, @opencode and other coding harnesses into RL environments. No changes to the harnesses, no changes to the training code. Any open model, any task set, fully open source my friends!

Same model, same weights: 62% under Mini-SWE-Agent, 33% under Claude Code. But training inside a real harness normally means reimplementing it as an environment, so most models get trained in a scaffold nobody actually ships.

The fix is a proxy, not a rewrite. The harness thinks it's talking to a model API. It's actually talking to a capture proxy that speaks the 4 formats coding agents use (OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, Gemini), forwards to @vllm_project, records the exact token IDs and logprobs vLLM sampled, and hands TRL sequences it can train on. The harness becomes the environment. 10 harnesses run through it today, none modified.

And because you control the reward, you can shape behavior the harness never asked for. We added a small bonus for solving a task in fewer tool calls: on tasks it already solved, the model now uses 31% fewer calls, in every harness, and about half under Codex.

Tested on LFM2.5-2.6B from @liquidai:
→ Train in one harness: better mostly in that harness (OpenCode 34% → 58%).
→ Train in 4 at once: better in all 4 (42% → 54%).
→ SFT on 3,189 rollouts from Qwen3.8-27B instead: plateaus at 47.5%, below both RL runs.

Everything is open and reproducible: the capture proxy in OpenEnv, the trainer in TRL, the tasks, the SFT data, the training code and all 7 trained models. Bigger models and bigger runs next.

Full guide: https://t.co/sKZURuOcza

1. STOP TRYING TO DO EVERYTHING.

AI content creation is ridiculously broad.

And one of the biggest mistakes I see beginners make is trying to learn everything at once.

Today you’re creating AI ads.

Tomorrow you’re creating music videos.

The next day you’re doing AI influencers.

Then animation.

Then storytelling.

Then product photography.

Then motion graphics.

Then podcasts.

Before you know it, you’ve touched 15 things and mastered absolutely nothing.

Even something like AI advertising has sub-niches.
You could specialize in:

UGC ads, cinematic commercials, product ads, fashion ads, real estate ads, food ads, storytelling commercials, e-commerce ads…

The same applies to AI storytelling, AI music, image generation and almost every other category.

Pick something.

Become ridiculously good at it.

Give yourself at least 90 days of focused execution before deciding it isn’t working.

You don’t need to become known for everything.

You need people to associate your name with something.
